h1: The 8 Best Vornado Space Heaters for Drafty Rooms and Cold Offices, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Vornado Space Heaters 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 Vornado space heaters compared on vortex circulation, smart sensing, safety shut-offs, oscillation and remote control.
summary: The Vornado TAVH10 is the best Vornado heater for most rooms, with a thermostat that senses how much heat is needed, an LCD, touch controls and a remote. The VMHI500 metal heater is the premium pick, the Velocity CUBE 5 OSC adds 70 degree oscillation, and the AVH10 is the smart-sensing option with a fan-only mode.
intro: Most space heaters warm the air around the heater and leave the rest of the room cold. You end up standing close to a glowing coil, which is neither comfortable nor especially safe. Vornado builds its heaters on the opposite idea, using a fan to circulate warm air through the space so the whole room evens out, and that difference in design is what this ranking explores.

We reviewed eight 2026-model Vornado heaters, from personal ceramic units to whole-room towers and cubes. They differ in how much they sense, whether they oscillate and how many controls they offer. Wattage and room-size ratings are mostly missing from the data we reviewed, so we rank on technology and safety features and urge you to check ratings on the retailer page.

products.name: Vornado TAVH10 (2026) Space Heater with Remote
products.verdict: Senses how much heat is needed, with an LCD, touch controls, a remote and ETL certification.
products.description:
The TAVH10 is a Vornado space heater that intelligently senses how much heat a room needs, with an LCD screen, touch-sensitive controls and a remote. It is ETL certified and has safety features including a cool-touch exterior. It costs $100 to $200.

It earns top place by being the most complete package. A sensing thermostat means the heater adjusts itself, so it neither overshoots nor cycles hard, and an LCD with a remote lets you set the room from your chair. ETL certification confirms it was tested to safety standards, which matters for any heater left running. The price is the top of the Vornado range, which is the tradeoff.

Buy it for a bedroom, office or den where you want to set a temperature and forget it. Skip it if you want the cheapest heater.
pros: Senses how much heat is needed
products.idealFor: Bedrooms and offices needing set-and-forget heat.
products.skipIf: You want the cheapest possible heater.

products.name: Vornado VMHI500 (2026) Metal Space Heater
products.verdict: A metal-bodied heater with vortex circulation, touch controls and a remote.
products.description:
The VMHI500 is a metal Vornado heater built around vortex heat circulation, with a safety-first design, touch-sensitive controls and an included remote. It costs $100 to $200.

Its metal body gives it a more durable, premium feel than the plastic models, and metal tends to hold up better to knocks in a busy household. Touch controls and a remote make it easy to adjust. It sits second because the listing does not mention thermostat sensing the way the TAVH10 does, so it may need more manual tweaking.

Buy it if you want a sturdy, good-looking heater with remote control. The metal body will feel warm after long use.
products.idealFor: Living rooms and offices that want a sturdy, handsome heater.

products.name: Vornado Velocity CUBE 5 OSC Whole Room Space Heater with 70o Oscillation
products.verdict: Velocity tuned heat with 70 degree oscillation for larger rooms and wider coverage.
products.description:
The Velocity CUBE 5 OSC is a whole-room heater that combines velocity-tuned heat technology with 70 degree oscillation. It has tip-over protection and automatic shut-off, and costs $100 to $200.

Oscillation is the feature that matters here: instead of aiming heat at one spot, it sweeps across a 70 degree arc, so more of the room gets warmed. The velocity-tuned design pushes heat farther than a plain fan heater. It trails the first two because the listing says nothing about remote or sensing.

Buy it for a living room or open space where heat must spread. It is less suited to a tiny bedroom.
products.idealFor: Living rooms and open spaces needing wide coverage.
products.skipIf: You need a small bedroom heater.

products.name: Vornado AVH10 (2026) Space Heater
products.verdict: A smart heater that senses heat needs, with two quiet settings and a fan-only mode.
products.description:
The AVH10 is a smart space heater that automatically senses how much heat a room needs, with vortex heat circulation for small to medium spaces. It has two quiet heat settings plus a fan-only mode, and costs $50 to $100.

A fan-only mode is a useful bonus, since it turns the heater into a year-round air circulator. Smart sensing gives much of what the TAVH10 offers at half the price. It lands fourth because it lacks the LCD, remote and ETL mention of the leader, and it is limited to small and medium rooms.

Buy it for a bedroom or small office where quiet matters. Choose the TAVH10 if you want the remote.
pros: Smart sensing at a mid price
cons: Limited to small and medium rooms
products.idealFor: Bedrooms and small offices wanting quiet, smart heat.
products.skipIf: You need a remote or larger room coverage.

products.name: Vornado VC-01 Ceramic Heater with Velocity Tuned Heat®
products.verdict: A ceramic heater with personal or whole-room modes, 15 degree tilt and a reusable pre-filter.
products.description:
The VC-01 is a ceramic heater with velocity tuned heat, selectable personal or whole-room modes, 15 degree tilt adjustment and a reusable pre-filter to reduce dust. It costs $50 to $100.

The selectable modes let one heater serve as a desk warmer or a room heater. The tilt adjustment aims warmth upward at your feet or legs, and the washable pre-filter cuts dust that builds up inside many fan heaters. It ranks fifth because it does not mention sensing or a remote.

Buy it for a desk or small room where you want flexible aim. A larger room needs a stronger model.
products.idealFor: Desks, studios and small rooms needing flexible aim.
products.skipIf: You want to heat a large room.

products.name: Vornado Rise 20H (2026) Whole Room Tower Heater
products.verdict: A sleek tower heater with three distinct heat settings for whole-room warmth.
products.description:
The Rise 20H is a Vornado whole-room tower heater with three distinct heat settings and a sleek design. A tower shape stands tall and narrow, taking less floor space than a box heater.

Towers push warm air upward and outward, which suits a bedroom corner or hallway where floor space is tight. Three heat settings give you more control than a two-step heater. It ranks sixth because the data we reviewed lists no price tier, sensing or remote, and tall units tip more easily if bumped.

Buy it for a narrow space where footprint matters. Confirm the price and safety features on the retailer page.
cons: Tall shape can tip if bumped
products.idealFor: Narrow rooms and corners with little floor space.
products.skipIf: You have pets or kids who may bump it.

products.name: Vornado MVH Space Heater (2026)
products.verdict: A vortex-circulation heater built for safe operation with three heat modes.
products.description:
The MVH is a Vornado heater that uses vortex heat circulation, is built for safe operation and offers three heat modes. It costs $50 to $100.

It places seventh because the listing is short on distinguishing features. Three heat modes and vortex circulation are the Vornado basics, and they work well in a small room, but there is no sensing, remote or oscillation to set it apart. It is a fair choice at its price.

Buy it for a basic, reliable room heater with Vornado's circulation design. Step up to the AVH10 for smart sensing.
products.idealFor: Small rooms needing a plain, dependable heater.

products.name: Vornado VH10 (2026) Space Heater
products.verdict: A two-setting heater with a cool-touch case and tip-over protection for small rooms.
products.description:
The VH10 is a Vornado heater for small spaces with two heat settings, a cool-touch case and tip-over protection. It costs $50 to $100.

It finishes last because two settings and no sensing make it the most basic in the group. The cool-touch case and tip-over protection are real safety wins for homes with children or pets. It heats small rooms efficiently by circulating air instead of just radiating.

Buy it for a bedroom, nursery or bathroom-adjacent room where simplicity and safety matter. Do not expect it to handle a large space.
products.idealFor: Small rooms with children or pets.
products.skipIf: You need to heat a larger space.

methodology.title: Circulation design
methodology.description: We favoured Vornado's vortex and velocity-tuned designs that move warm air around a room instead of heating one spot.

methodology.title: Sensing and controls
methodology.description: Thermostat sensing, LCD displays, touch controls and remotes were credited for set-and-forget comfort.

methodology.title: Safety features
methodology.description: Tip-over protection, automatic shut-off, cool-touch cases and ETL certification were weighed heavily for any heater left on.

methodology.title: Coverage and oscillation
methodology.description: Oscillation, tower shapes and personal versus whole-room modes were matched to room sizes.

methodology.title: Value
methodology.description: Price tiers of $50 to $200 were set against features, with missing wattage and room ratings counted as a gap.

whatMatters.detail: A Vornado heater uses a fan to swirl warm air through the room, reducing hot and cold pockets. This makes a small heater feel more effective than a plain radiant one. Look for the words vortex or velocity tuned in the listing.

A sensing heater measures room temperature and adjusts output, so it holds a steady warmth and uses less power. Without it, you control the settings yourself. Check for words like senses or intelligent in the listing.

Tip-over protection shuts the heater off if it falls, automatic shut-off prevents overheating, and a cool-touch case guards against burns. ETL or UL certification confirms testing. Plug heaters directly into a wall outlet, not an extension cord.
Oscillation sweeps heat across a wider area, and tilt directs warmth where you sit. Both help when the heater sits off to one side. Look for stated angles, such as 70 degrees or 15 degrees.
A remote lets you adjust from bed or a couch, and quiet settings help in bedrooms. LCD and touch controls are easy to read. Check noise claims, since fan heaters hum.

howToChoose.intro: Match the heater to the room, because a small unit in a big space just runs without ever warming it.

cards.label: Smart sensing
cards.text: The heater reads the room and adjusts itself. The Vornado TAVH10 and AVH10 work this way, and they keep temperature steadier with less fuss.

cards.label: Manual settings
cards.text: You choose the heat level yourself. The MVH, VH10, VC-01 and Rise 20H use this approach, which is simpler and cheaper.

howToChoose.note: Choose smart sensing for bedrooms and offices, and manual settings for occasional use.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Quiet heat settings, a cool-touch case, tip-over protection and automatic sensing. A remote helps you adjust from bed.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Vornado AVH10 is the best bedroom value, and the TAVH10 adds a remote. The VH10 is the safest basic option.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: The heater will run daily or in a larger room. The Vornado TAVH10 and VMHI500 at $100 to $200 add sensing, controls and build.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You need heat for a few cold evenings. The VH10 or MVH at $50 to $100 are enough.

faq.q: Can I leave a Vornado heater on overnight?
faq.a: Follow the manual. These heaters have tip-over protection and automatic shut-off, but any space heater should be placed on a flat floor away from bedding and curtains. Never use an extension cord.

faq.q: What is the common mistake with space heaters?
faq.a: Buying one that is too small for the room, or placing it where air flow is blocked. Check the room size and keep three feet of clearance around the heater.

faq.q: Is a smart-sensing model worth it over a basic one?
faq.a: For daily use, yes. Sensing holds the room temperature and avoids constant manual changes. For occasional use, a basic model costs less.

faq.q: How do I set up the heater?
faq.a: Place it on a flat, hard surface, plug it into a wall outlet and set the heat level. Keep it clear of cords, fabric and furniture. Use the remote if one is provided.
Unplug and let it cool. Vacuum the grille, and wash the pre-filter on the VC-01 if fitted. Never use water inside the unit.

faq.q: Can I use it in a bathroom?
faq.a: Only if the manual allows it, and most space heaters are not designed for wet areas. Keep them away from sinks and showers. A bathroom-rated heater is a safer choice.

finalTake: The Vornado TAVH10 is the best heater here for anyone who wants sensing, a remote and certified safety in one unit. The VMHI500 is the sturdy metal alternative, and the Velocity CUBE 5 OSC covers larger rooms with 70 degree oscillation. For small rooms, the AVH10 offers smart sensing at a lower price, while the VH10 keeps things basic and safe.
